#### About the challenge

PayPal already moves money for millions of people and businesses, every day, all over the world. This hackathon is us opening that platform up and asking what happens when you put AI behind the wheel. New agents, new ways to pay and get paid, tools nobody's built yet. We want to see what you make of it.

AI is changing how people build, buy, sell, work, connect, and move money. Now it's your turn to imagine what comes next.

Build What's Next with PayPal and AI is a global online hackathon inviting developers, designers, founders, students, and builders to create something new using PayPal and AI .

There are no prescribed problem statements and no set of tracks. Build an agent, an app, an automation, a new payment experience, a business tool, a social product, or something we haven't thought of yet.

The only fundamental requirement: your project must meaningfully use both PayPal and AI .

#### Why Join?

-
Build something ambitious — Turn an idea into a working project using PayPal and AI.

-
Explore what’s next — Experiment with new ways people, businesses, and AI agents can interact with money and payments.

-
Win part of $ 69,750 in total prizes — Compete for overall prizes and special awards across creativity, impact, execution, and more.

-
Show what you can build — Put your project in front of PayPal judges, developers, and the wider hackathon community.

-
Learn by building — Explore PayPal APIs, AI tools, agents, automations, and emerging development workflows.

-
Build your way — Join individually or as a team, and start something new or meaningfully advance an existing project.

#### Get started

-
Get a PayPal Developer account (5 minutes)

-
Review example projects and brainstorm your own (30 minutes)

### Requirements

#### What to Build

Build or update an application that integrates the PayPal developer platform (using the free sandbox environment) along with an AI tool, model, or platform of your choice.

You may also use one of our sponsors' tools:

- AG Grid

- APIMatic

- Astropods

- Bryntum

- Channel3

- Elastic

- KERNEL

- Postman

- Render

- Zapier

Note: PayPal will provide access to select AI sponsor tools that you are welcome to use, though using one of these partner tools is not required. Any AI tool works, as long as PayPal integration is central to the project.

Your project should:

- Meaningfully integrate at least one PayPal technology, API, SDK, product, or developer capability

- Meaningfully incorporate AI into the experience or functionality

- Demonstrate a working prototype or proof of concept

- Be sufficiently documented for the judges to understand and evaluate it

- Comply with the Official Rules

Projects can be built individually or as a team. They can be new or existing projects, as long as you make meaningful progress on the project during the course of the hackathon.

-
Project - built with the required developer tools and meeting the Project Requirements above.

-
Text description - explain your project's features and functionality.

-

-

-

-

SUBMISSION OF ANY ENTRY CONSTITUTES AGREEMENT TO THESE OFFICIAL RULES AS A CONTRACT BETWEEN ENTRANT (AND EACH INDIVIDUAL MEMBER OF ENTRANT), THE HACKATHON SPONSOR, AND DEVPOST.

#### 1. Dates and Timing

Submission Period: Thursday Oct 1, 2026 (9:15 am Pacific Time) – Thursday Nov 12, 2026 (12:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Submission Period”).

Judging Period: Tuesday Dec 1, 2026 (2:00 pm Pacific Time) – Tuesday Dec 15, 2026 (8:00 am Pacific Time) (“Judging Period”).

#### 3. Eligibility

-

-

-
Teams of Eligible Individuals (“Teams”); and

-
Organizations (including corporations, not-for-profit corporations and other nonprofit organizations, limited liability companies, partnerships, and other legal entities) that exist and have been organized or incorporated at the time of entry.

(the above are collectively, “Entrants”)

An Eligible Individual may join more than one Team or Organization and an Eligible Individual who is part of a Team or Organization may also enter the Hackathon on an individual basis. If a Team or Organization is entering the Hackathon, they must appoint and authorize one individual (the “Representative”) to represent, act, and enter a Submission, on their behalf. By entering a Submission on behalf of a Team or Organization you represent and warrant that you are the Representative authorized to act on behalf of your Team or Organization.

-
The Hackathon IS NOT open to:

-
Individuals who are residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, province or territory where the laws of the United States or local law prohibits participating or receiving a prize in the Hackathon (including, but not limited to, Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, and North Korea and any other country which is comprehensively sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control)

-
Organizations involved with the design, production, paid promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, including the Sponsor and Administrator (“Promotion Entities”).

-
Employees, representatives and agents** of such Promotion Entities, and all members of their immediate family or household*

-
Any other individual involved with the design, production, promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, and each member of their immediate family or household*

-
Any Judge (defined below), or company or individual that employs a Judge

-
Any parent company, subsidiary, or other affiliate*** of any organization described above

-
Any other individual or organization whose participation in the Hackathon would create, in the sole discretion of the Sponsor and/or Administrator, a real or apparent conflict of interest

#### 4. How To Enter

Entrants may enter by visiting paypalaihackathon.devpost.com (“Hackathon Website”) and following the below steps:

-

-

Entry in the Hackathon constitutes consent for the Sponsor and Devpost to collect and maintain an entrant’s personal information for the purpose of operating and publicizing the Hackathon.

-
To access the PayPal sandbox environment, use your existing PayPal account or create a free account at https://developer.paypal.com/ .

-

Project Requirements

-

-
This includes all the services provided by PayPal such as Venmo, Braintree, Xoom, Honey, Zettle, Paidy, Hyperwallet, Simility, Swift Financial, and others.

-
New & Existing: Projects must be either newly created by the Entrant or, if the Entrant’s Project existed prior to the Hackathon Submission Period, must have been significantly updated after the start of the Hackathon Submission Period. Entrants should explain how their Project was significantly updated during the Submission Period. Sponsor and Administrator will determine what constitutes a “significant change” at their sole discretion.

-
Third Party Integrations: If a Project integrates any third-party SDK, APIs and/or data, Entrant must be authorized to use them in accordance with any terms and conditions or licensing requirements of the tool.

Submission Requirements

Submissions to the Hackathon must meet the following requirements:

-
Include a Project built with the required developer tools and meets the above Project Requirements.

-
Include a text description that should explain the features and functionality of your Project.

-

Language Requirements

Team Representation

#### 6. Judges & Criteria

This process may utilize expert panels, peer review, automated AI-driven analysis, or any combination thereof to ensure efficient, fair, and objective evaluation. Eligible submissions will be evaluated by a panel of judges selected by the Sponsor (the “Judges”). Judges may be employees of the sponsor or third parties, may or may not be listed individually on the Hackathon Website, and may change before or during the Judging Period. Judging may take place in one or more rounds with one or more panels of Judges, at the discretion of the sponsor.

Stage One) The first stage will determine via pass/fail whether the ideas meet a baseline level of viability, in that the Project reasonably fits the theme and reasonably applies the required APIs/SDKs featured in the Hackathon.

Stage Two) All Submissions that pass Stage One will be evaluated in Stage Two based on the following equally weighted criteria (the “Judging Criteria”):

Entries will be judged on the following equally weighted criteria, and according to the sole and absolute discretion of the judges:

-
Technological Implementation: How thoroughly and skillfully does the project use PayPal Developer Platform and AI tool(s)? Does the project reflect genuine effort and a working, non-trivial implementation?

-
Design: Does the project deliver a complete, coherent product experience — not just a technical proof of concept?

-
Potential Impact: Does the project make a credible, specific case for solving a real problem for a real audience — and does the solution actually address that problem based on what's demonstrated?

-
Innovation/Idea: How creative and novel is the concept and does the project differ from existing concepts?

-
Presentation: Does the video clearly demonstrate the project working end-to-end? Does the pitch communicate what problem is solved, who it's for, and why it matters? Is the overall presentation easy to follow?

The scores from the Judges will determine the potential winners of the applicable prizes. The Entrant(s) that are eligible for a Prize, and whose Submissions earn the highest overall scores based on the applicable Judging Criteria, will become potential winners of that Prize.

For each Prize listed below, if two or more Submissions are tied, the tied Submission with the highest score in the first applicable criterion listed above will be considered the higher scoring Submission. In the event any ties remain, this process will be repeated, as needed, by comparing the tied Submissions’ scores on the next applicable criterion. If two or more Submissions are tied on all applicable criteria, the panel of Judges will vote on the tied Submissions.

#### PayPal AI Hackathon (the “Hackathon”) Official Rules

NO PURCHASE OR PAYMENT NECESSARY TO ENTER OR WIN. A PURCHASE OR PAYMENT WILL NOT INCREASE YOUR CHANCES OF WINNING.

SUBMISSION OF ANY ENTRY CONSTITUTES AGREEMENT TO THESE OFFICIAL RULES AS A CONTRACT BETWEEN ENTRANT (AND EACH INDIVIDUAL MEMBER OF ENTRANT), THE HACKATHON SPONSOR, AND DEVPOST.

#### 1. Dates and Timing

Judging Period: Tuesday Dec 1, 2026 (2:00 pm Pacific Time) – Tuesday Dec 15, 2026 (8:00 am Pacific Time) (“Judging Period”).

#### 3. Eligibility

-

-
Individuals who are at least the age of majority where they reside as of the time of entry (“Eligible Individuals”);

-
Teams of Eligible Individuals (“Teams”); and

-
Organizations (including corporations, not-for-profit corporations and other nonprofit organizations, limited liability companies, partnerships, and other legal entities) that exist and have been organized or incorporated at the time of entry.

(the above are collectively, “Entrants”)

An Eligible Individual may join more than one Team or Organization and an Eligible Individual who is part of a Team or Organization may also enter the Hackathon on an individual basis. If a Team or Organization is entering the Hackathon, they must appoint and authorize one individual (the “Representative”) to represent, act, and enter a Submission, on their behalf. By entering a Submission on behalf of a Team or Organization you represent and warrant that you are the Representative authorized to act on behalf of your Team or Organization.

-
The Hackathon IS NOT open to:

-
Individuals who are residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, province or territory where the laws of the United States or local law prohibits participating or receiving a prize in the Hackathon (including, but not limited to, Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, and North Korea and any other country which is comprehensively sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control)

-
Organizations involved with the design, production, paid promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, including the Sponsor and Administrator (“Promotion Entities”).

-
Employees, representatives and agents** of such Promotion Entities, and all members of their immediate family or household*

-
Any other individual involved with the design, production, promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, and each member of their immediate family or household*

-
Any Judge (defined below), or company or individual that employs a Judge

-
Any parent company, subsidiary, or other affiliate*** of any organization described above

Any other individual or organization whose participation in the Hackathon would create, in the sole discretion of the Sponsor and/or Administrator, a real or apparent conflict of interest

#### 4. How To Enter

Entrants may enter by visiting paypalaihackathon.devpost.com (“Hackathon Website”) and following the below steps:

-
Register for the Hackathon on the Hackathon Website by clicking the “Join Hackathon” button. To complete registration, sign up to create a free Devpost account, or log in with an existing Devpost account. This will enable you to receive important updates and to create your Submission.

-
Entrants will obtain access to the required developer tools/platform and complete a Project described below in Project Requirements. Use of the developer tools will be subject to the license agreement related thereto. Entry in the Hackathon constitutes consent for the Sponsor and Devpost to collect and maintain an entrant’s personal information for the purpose of operating and publicizing the Hackathon.

-
To access the PayPal sandbox environment, use your existing PayPal account or create a free account at https://developer.paypal.com/ .

-
Complete and enter all of the required fields on the “Enter a Submission” page of the Hackathon Website (each a “Submission”) during the Submission Period and follow the requirements below.

Project Requirements

-
What to Create: Entrants must build or update an application that integrates the PayPal developer platform (using the free sandbox environment) along with an AI tool, model, or platform of their choice (each a “Project”).

-
This includes all the services provided by PayPal such as Venmo, Braintree, Xoom, Honey, Zettle, Paidy, Hyperwallet, Simility, Swift Financial, and others.

-
PayPal will provide access to select AI sponsor tools that entrants are welcome to use, though using one of these partner tools is not required. Any AI tool works, as long as PayPal integration is central to the project.

-
Functionality: The Project must be capable of being successfully installed and running consistently on the platform for which it is intended and must function as depicted in the video and/or expressed in the text description.

-
Platforms: A submitted Project must run on the platform for which it is intended and which is specified in the Submission Requirements.

-
New & Existing: Projects must be either newly created by the Entrant or, if the Entrant’s Project existed prior to the Hackathon Submission Period, must have been significantly updated after the start of the Hackathon Submission Period. Entrants should explain how their Project was significantly updated during the Submission Period. Sponsor and Administrator will determine what constitutes a “significant change” at their sole discretion.

-
Third Party Integrations: If a Project integrates any third-party SDK, APIs and/or data, Entrant must be authorized to use them in accordance with any terms and conditions or licensing requirements of the tool.

Submission Requirements

Submissions to the Hackathon must meet the following requirements:

-
Include a Project built with the required developer tools and meets the above Project Requirements.

-
Include a text description that should explain the features and functionality of your Project.

-
Provide access to a functional demo of your application. Your project does not need to be publicly hosted or deployed — but judges must be able to actually run or interact with a working build.

-
This can be satisfied through clear, complete setup and run instructions in your code repository (so judges can build and run it themselves) OR

-
A hosted demo URL.

-
A design mockup, static prototype, or non-functional demo does not meet this requirement.

-
Provide a URL to your public code repository for judging and testing on GitHub, Bitbucket, or Gitlab.

-
The repository must contain all necessary source code, assets, and instructions required for the project to be functional.

-
The repository must be public and open source by including an open source license file. This license should be detectable and visible at the top of the repository page (in the About section).

-

-
should be less than three (3) minutes. Judges are not required to watch beyond three minutes

-
should include footage that shows the Project functioning on the device for which it was built

-
must be uploaded to and made publicly visible on YouTube and a link to the video must be provided on the submission form on the Hackathon Website; and

-
must not include third party trademarks, or copyrighted music or other material unless the Entrant has permission to use such material.

Multiple Submissions

An Entrant may submit more than one Submission, however, each Submission must be unique and substantially different from each of the Entrant’s other Submissions, as determined by the Sponsor and Devpost in their sole discretion.

Submission ownership

Be the original work of the Entrant, be solely owned by the Entrant, and not violate the IP rights of any other person or entity.

Testing

Access must be provided to an Entrant’s working Project for judging and testing by providing a link to a website, functioning demo, or a test build. If Entrant’s website is private, Entrant must include login credentials in its testing instructions. The Entrant must make the Project available free of charge and without any restriction, for testing, evaluation and use by the Sponsor, Administrator and Judges until the Judging Period ends. Judges are not required to test the Project and may choose to judge based solely on the text description, images, and video provided in the Submission.

Access can be provided to the Sponsor and Administrator by including complete setup and run instructions in your project's code repository (see Repository Requirements above), along with any test account credentials, API keys, or sandbox login details necessary to run and test the Project. If your submission requires special access, please include clear instructions for obtaining access within your repository's README or project description.

If the Project includes software that runs on proprietary or third party hardware that is not widely available to the public, including software running on devices or wearable technology other than smartphones, tablets, or desktop computers, the Sponsor and/or Administrator reserve the right, at their sole discretion, to require the Entrant to provide physical access to the Project hardware upon request.

Language Requirements

All Submission materials must be in English or, if not in English, the Entrant must provide an English translation of the demonstration video, text description, and testing instructions as well as all other materials submitted.

Team Representation

If a team or organization is entering the Hackathon, they must appoint and authorize one individual (the “Representative”) to represent, act, and enter a Submission, on their behalf. The Representative must meet the eligibility requirements above. By entering a Submission on the Hackathon Website on behalf of a team or organization you represent and warrant that you are the Representative authorized to act on behalf of your team or organization.

Intellectual Property

Your Submission must: (a) be your (or your Team, or Organization’s) original work product; (b) be solely owned by you, your Team, your Organization with no other person or entity having any right or interest in it; and (c) not violate the intellectual property rights or other rights including but not limited to copyright, trademark, patent, contract, and/or privacy rights, of any other person or entity. An Entrant may contract with a third party for technical assistance to create the Submission provided the Submission components are solely the Entrant’s work product and the result of the Entrant’s ideas and creativity, and the Entrant owns all rights to them. An Entrant may submit a Submission that includes the use of open source software or hardware, provided the Entrant complies with applicable open source licenses and, as part of the Submission, creates software that enhances and builds upon the features and functionality included in the underlying open source product. By entering the Hackathon, you represent, warrant, and agree that your Submission meets these requirements.

Financial or Preferential Support

A Project must not have been developed, or derived from a Project developed, with financial or preferential support from the Sponsor or Administrator. Such Projects include, but are not limited to, those that received funding or investment for their development, were developed under contract, or received a commercial license, from the Sponsor or Administrator any time prior to the end of Hackathon Submission Period. The Sponsor, at their sole discretion, may disqualify a Project, if awarding a prize to the Project would create a real or apparent conflict of interest.

#### 5. Submission Modifications

Draft Submissions

Prior to the end of the Submission Period, you may save draft versions of your submission on Devpost to your portfolio before submitting the Submission materials to the Hackathon for evaluation. Once the Submission Period has ended, you may not make any changes or alterations to your Submission, but you may continue to update the Project in your Devpost portfolio.

Modifications After the Submission Period

The Sponsor and Devpost may permit you to modify part of your Submission after the Submission Period for the purpose of adding, removing or replacing material that potentially infringes a third party mark or right, discloses personally identifiable information, or is otherwise inappropriate. The modified Submission must remain substantively the same as the original Submission with the only modification being what the Sponsor and Devpost permits.

#### 6. Judges & Criteria

Sponsor and Administrator reserve the sole right to determine the eligibility and judging methodologies for all submissions. This process may utilize expert panels, peer review, automated AI-driven analysis, or any combination thereof to ensure efficient, fair, and objective evaluation. Eligible submissions will be evaluated by a panel of judges selected by the Sponsor (the “Judges”). Judges may be employees of the sponsor or third parties, may or may not be listed individually on the Hackathon Website, and may change before or during the Judging Period. Judging may take place in one or more rounds with one or more panels of Judges, at the discretion of the sponsor.

Stage One) The first stage will determine via pass/fail whether the ideas meet a baseline level of viability, in that the Project reasonably fits the theme and reasonably applies the required APIs/SDKs featured in the Hackathon.

Stage Two) All Submissions that pass Stage One will be evaluated in Stage Two based on the following equally weighted criteria (the “Judging Criteria”):

Entries will be judged on the following equally weighted criteria, and according to the sole and absolute discretion of the judges:

-
Technological Implementation: How thoroughly and skillfully does the project use PayPal Developer Platform and AI tool(s)? Does the project reflect genuine effort and a working, non-trivial implementation?

-
Design: Does the project deliver a complete, coherent product experience — not just a technical proof of concept?

-
Potential Impact: Does the project make a credible, specific case for solving a real problem for a real audience — and does the solution actually address that problem based on what's demonstrated?

-
Innovation/Idea: How creative and novel is the concept and does the project differ from existing concepts?

-
Presentation: Does the video clearly demonstrate the project working end-to-end? Does the pitch communicate what problem is solved, who it's for, and why it matters? Is the overall presentation easy to follow?

The scores from the Judges will determine the potential winners of the applicable prizes. The Entrant(s) that are eligible for a Prize, and whose Submissions earn the highest overall scores based on the applicable Judging Criteria, will become potential winners of that Prize.

Tie Breaking

For each Prize listed below, if two or more Submissions are tied, the tied Submission with the highest score in the first applicable criterion listed above will be considered the higher scoring Submission. In the event any ties remain, this process will be repeated, as needed, by comparing the tied Submissions’ scores on the next applicable criterion. If two or more Submissions are tied on all applicable criteria, the panel of Judges will vote on the tied Submissions.

By submitting an entry, entrants agree that the Sponsor will have a non-exclusive license to use such entry for judging the entry. Entrants agree that the sponsor and Devpost shall have the right to promote the Submission and use the name, likeness, voice and image of all individuals contributing to a Submission, in any materials promoting or publicizing the Hackathon and its results, during the Hackathon Period and for three years thereafter. Some Submission components may be displayed to the public. Other Submission materials may be viewed by the sponsor, Devpost, and judges for screening and evaluation. By submitting an entry or accepting any prize, entrants represent and warrant that (a) submitted content is not copyrighted, protected by trade secret or otherwise subject to third party intellectual property rights or other proprietary rights, including privacy and publicity rights, unless entrant is the owner of such rights or has permission from their rightful owner to post the content; and (b) the content submitted does not contain any viruses, Trojan horses, worms, spyware or other disabling devices or harmful or malicious code.

## What's next for QuickInvoice — Smart Invoice Manager for Freelancers

## The Problem

Freelancers lose thousands every year to late payments and forgotten invoices. Most use WhatsApp to confirm work, Excel to track payments, and Google Docs to create invoices. It's a mess of tabs, and money slips through the cracks.

I've felt this myself as a solo developer. Chasing payments is exhausting. There had to be a better way.

## What QuickInvoice Does

QuickInvoice is a clean, fast invoice manager built specifically for freelancers and solo service providers. In under 2 minutes you can:

- Create a professional invoice with line items and auto-calculated totals

- Track payment status from Draft → Sent → Viewed → Partial → Paid

- Get instant visibility on overdue invoices before they slip through

- Manage your entire client directory in one place

- See your business health at a glance — revenue, outstanding, overdue count

No bloat. No complexity. Just the tools you actually need to get paid.

## How I Built It — Powered by MeDo

Built entirely using MeDo — no code written manually. Here's exactly how I used MeDo's features to ship a production-ready app:

### Prompt Optimization

Instead of jumping straight into building, I described my idea in plain English. MeDo's prompt optimization took my rough concept and automatically generated a structured full-stack requirements document — covering database schema, API design, UI component breakdown, auth flow, and edge cases.

What would have taken me hours of architecture planning happened in minutes. The requirements.md MeDo generated became the blueprint for the entire app.

### Skills — Modern UI Upgrade

The first generation was functional but looked basic. I used MeDo's Skills feature to upgrade the entire UI to a modern SaaS design.

The result:

- Split-panel login with dark sidebar and social proof

- Monospace animated revenue numbers on the dashboard

- Color-coded status badges (Draft, Sent, Viewed, Partial Payment, Paid)

- Clean invoice list with overdue dates highlighted in red

- Responsive layout that works on any screen

No manual CSS. No design iterations. Skills handled it in one pass.

### Stripe Integration

Integrated Stripe for subscription billing directly through MeDo. The billing page, payment flow, and webhook handling were all generated and connected without writing a single line of payment code.

Freelancers can subscribe to a Pro plan for advanced features — all powered by Stripe under the hood, set up through a simple MeDo prompt.

### Early Testing

Used MeDo's built-in testing features to catch bugs before publishing.

The most critical tests were around invoice calculations — tax rates applied on top of discounts, partial payment tracking, and overdue date detection. MeDo's test runner confirmed all edge cases were handled correctly.

Without this I would have shipped a calculator that silently gave wrong totals. Early testing caught it before any real user saw it.

## What the App Looks Like

- Landing page — clear value prop, features, reviews, FAQ, pricing

- Auth — modern split-screen login with feature highlights

- Dashboard — total revenue, outstanding, overdue count, recent invoices

- Clients — searchable client cards with full contact details

- Invoices — filterable list with status badges and overdue highlighting

- New Invoice — client selector, line items, tax, discount, auto-total

- Billing — Stripe-powered subscription management

## What I Learned

MeDo works dramatically better when you describe the problem from the user's perspective , not the technical one.

"Freelancers lose track of who owes them money" produced a much better app than "build a CRUD app with PostgreSQL." The prompt optimization feature reinforced this — it translated my user-focused description into precise technical requirements automatically.

The Skills feature taught me that design polish isn't about tweaking CSS line by line. Describing the aesthetic you want — "modern SaaS, dark sidebar, monospace numbers" — and letting MeDo's Skills execute it is faster and better than doing it manually.

## Challenges

Overdue detection — Getting invoices to flag correctly required a follow-up prompt. The initial version only checked due date, not payment status combined with due date. A partial payment past due date should still show as overdue. MeDo fixed the database query logic cleanly on the second pass.

Calculation edge cases — Tax applied after discount vs before discount produced different totals. The early testing feature surfaced this immediately. One prompt fix resolved it for all invoice types.

## Inspiration

Freelancers lose real money to late payments — not because clients refuse to pay, but because chasing is awkward, so it doesn't happen. Invoicing tools are good at sending invoices; nobody helps with the part after the due date, where the relationship matters as much as the amount.

## What it does

- Bill from a conversation. Paste the email or chat where a client agreed to work. The agent extracts client, line items, rates, quantities, currency and terms, and creates a PayPal draft invoice.

- A collections queue ranked by risk. Each open invoice gets a 0–100 score from days overdue, amount, and that client's own history with you (on-time rate, average days late).

- Reminders written for the relationship. A reliable long-time client four days late gets a warm nudge; a repeat late payer three weeks over gets a firm note with a date; a client who has gone quiet gets a polite final notice.

- Human in the loop. Anything that emails a client — send, remind, cancel — lands in an approval queue. One click and PayPal sends it with a pay link. An Autopilot switch lets the agent act directly.

- Ask anything: "Who owes me money?", "Chase everyone overdue", "Tom paid by bank transfer, record it", "Cash-flow summary".

- Live payments. A signature-verified PayPal webhook updates the board when a client pays.

## How we built it

- PayPal Invoicing v2 is the system of record — Ledgerbird has no database. We use generate-next-invoice-number, create draft, send, remind, cancel, delete, record external payment, list and show invoice details, plus Webhooks with verify-webhook-signature (INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID/UPDATED/CANCELLED/REFUNDED ), all against the sandbox with OAuth client credentials.

- AI: a tool-calling agent over seven PayPal tools (get_ledger , create_invoice_draft , send_invoice , send_reminder , record_offline_payment , cancel_invoice , delete_draft ). Client-facing tools are intercepted into approval cards unless Autopilot is on. Model: Google Gemini via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with automatic fallback when a model is overloaded.

- Risk & tone engine: deterministic Python (app/ledger.py ) computes per-client payment profiles from PayPal history and picks the reminder tone the model must follow — the AI writes, the numbers decide.

- Stack: FastAPI, vanilla JS/CSS (no build step), hosted on Render .

## Challenges we ran into

- The invoice list endpoint returns summaries without payment transactions, so "days to pay" was always zero; we fetch full details concurrently and cache invoices that can no longer change.

- Back-dated invoices were essential for a realistic demo of overdue accounts; the sandbox accepts past invoice and payment dates, so the seed script recreates months of client history.

- Keeping an autonomous agent safe around client email: we made approval the default and Autopilot opt-in.

## Accomplishments that we're proud of

The agent is grounded entirely in live PayPal data, and every action it takes is a real PayPal API call you can see in the sandbox.

## What we learned

Most of the value in collections is judgement — who to chase, when, and how — not the email itself. Putting the judgement in transparent code and the wording in the model works better than asking the model to do both.

## What's next

Scheduled follow-ups, partial-payment plans, multi-currency reporting, and PayPal Payouts for paying subcontractors when a client's invoice clears.

## Tools used

- PayPal Invoicing v2 REST API — create/send/remind/cancel/record payments; source of truth for all data.

- PayPal Webhooks — real-time paid/updated/cancelled events, verified with verify-webhook-signature.

- PayPal sandbox — business account with seeded demo clients.

- Google Gemini (OpenAI-compatible API) — tool-calling agent, invoice extraction, reminder writing.

- Render — hosting (sponsor tool).

- Live demo: https://ledgerbird.onrender.com (free instance; first load can take ~50 s)

Open the live demo: the board is pre-populated with sandbox clients who pay on time, pay late, or have gone quiet. Try "Who owes me?", "Chase overdue" (then Approve one card), and "Bill from an email" followed by "send it". Everything runs on the PayPal sandbox; no real money moves.

# AI for Invoice and Payment Collection: How Small Agencies Get Paid Faster

By Joshua Mason • July 21, 2026

Drafted with AI assistance and reviewed before publishing.

AI-powered invoicing tools can automatically generate invoices, send payment reminders on a set schedule, predict which clients are likely to pay late, and flag overdue accounts for follow-up without any manual effort from you. For small agencies and consultancies, this means getting paid faster without spending hours chasing clients or managing uncomfortable payment conversations. The biggest gains come not from creating invoices faster but from eliminating the follow-up gaps that let invoices go 30, 60, or 90 days without payment.

## Why Do Small Agencies Struggle to Collect Payments on Time?

Getting paid late is not a minor inconvenience for a small agency. It creates real cash flow gaps that force you to cover payroll and expenses from reserves while waiting on client payments that should have cleared weeks ago.

The QuickBooks 2026 Small Business Late Payments Report found that 59% of small businesses have overdue invoices, with an average of $17,700 sitting unpaid at any given time. Nearly three in five businesses say at least some invoices are overdue by 30 days or more, up from 47% the previous year. And 51% of businesses with overdue invoices report that cash flow is a genuine problem as a direct result.

The root cause is usually not that clients intend to pay late. It is that most small agency billing workflows rely on the owner to manually track outstanding invoices, remember to follow up, and find the time to send a second or third reminder. When you are also doing client work, that follow-up slips. A client who would have paid on day 10 with a reminder instead pays on day 45 when you finally get around to it. AI closes that gap by making follow-up automatic.

## What Can AI Do for Invoicing and Payment Collection?

AI adds several capabilities that go beyond what basic invoicing software provides:

- Automated invoice creation. Connect your project management or CRM data and invoices generate automatically when a milestone or billing date is reached, including the correct line items, without manual entry.

- Payment reminder sequences. Set up a rule once: remind the client three days before the due date, again on the due date, and then escalate the message tone at 7, 14, and 30 days past due. The system sends every message automatically based on each invoice's status.

- Predictive payment timing. AI can analyze each client's historical payment behavior and flag invoices that are likely to go overdue before they actually do, so you can reach out earlier and avoid the delay entirely.

- Client payment portals. Self-serve portals let clients pay by credit card, ACH, or bank transfer in one click from the reminder email. Removing friction from the payment step is one of the most reliable ways to cut days-sales-outstanding (DSO).

- Collections prioritization. When multiple invoices are overdue, AI ranks them by value, client risk score, and days outstanding so your follow-up time goes to the accounts most likely to move with a nudge.

According to Parseur's 2026 AI Invoice Processing Benchmarks , manual invoice processing can cost between $12 and $19 per invoice when you factor in staff time. Automation brings that down to $3 to $6 per invoice, an 80% reduction for teams that invoice frequently.

## Manual vs. AI-Assisted Billing: A Side-by-Side Look

Step |

Manual approach |

AI-assisted approach |

Invoice creation |

Build each invoice manually in accounting software |

Invoice generated automatically from project or CRM data |

Sending invoices |

Email manually, sometimes delayed |

Sent automatically on trigger (milestone, date, or completion) |

Payment reminders |

Owner remembers and sends manually, often late |

Reminder sequence fires automatically at set intervals |

Overdue tracking |

Review spreadsheet or accounting dashboard periodically |

AI flags and prioritizes overdue accounts in real time |

Payment processing |

Client receives invoice and figures out how to pay |

One-click payment portal embedded in reminder email |

Reconciliation |

Match payments manually to invoices in accounting software |

Auto-matched and synced with QuickBooks or Xero |

## Which Tools Work Best for Small Agency Invoicing and Collections?

The right tool depends on whether you need an all-in-one invoicing system or an AR automation layer on top of your existing accounting software.

- FreshBooks. Best for service-based agencies that invoice by project or retainer. FreshBooks includes automated payment reminders, late fees, and a client portal. Its recurring invoice feature handles monthly retainers automatically. Strong for teams under 10 people who want everything in one place.

- HoneyBook. Designed for client-based service businesses. Combines contracts, invoices, and payments in one flow so you can send a proposal, get it signed, and collect a deposit in a single client interaction. Good for agencies that want to connect the sales and billing process.

- BILL (formerly Bill.com). Strong for agencies with multiple vendors and clients. Offers AI-powered invoice matching and automated AR workflows that integrate with QuickBooks and Xero. Better suited for teams with more complex multi-entity billing than FreshBooks.

- Melio. Focused on payment flexibility: lets clients pay by credit card even if you prefer ACH, absorbing or passing through card fees. Useful for agencies whose clients prefer to pay by card. Integrates with QuickBooks.

- Quadient AR. Enterprise-grade AR automation with predictive collections and cash flow forecasting. Quadient reports a 34% reduction in DSO for organizations using its AI-assisted AR workflows. Better suited for agencies billing above $500K annually that need advanced forecasting and dispute management.

Most agencies under 10 people will get the most impact from FreshBooks or HoneyBook with automated reminders enabled, rather than moving to a dedicated AR platform. Once you have a consistent billing workflow in place, our post on AI for bookkeeping and accounting covers how to connect that payment data to automated reconciliation and reporting.

## How Do You Set Up an Automated Invoice and Collections Workflow?

Here is a practical setup sequence for a small agency starting from scratch:

- Standardize your billing triggers. Decide exactly when invoices go out: on project completion, on the first of each month for retainers, or at defined milestones. Write these down as rules before touching any software. Automation only works reliably when the trigger is clearly defined.

- Choose your invoicing platform and connect it to your CRM or project tool. If you use ClickUp, Asana, or Monday.com for project tracking, most invoicing tools have direct integrations or Zapier/Make connectors so invoices generate automatically when a project status changes to complete.

- Write three reminder templates. Template 1: a friendly pre-due-date reminder sent 3 days before. Template 2: a polite post-due follow-up sent 3 to 5 days after the due date. Template 3: a firm escalation sent 14 to 21 days past due. Keep them short and professional. Our workflow automation service can help you build and connect these sequences across your billing and CRM stack.

- Enable a client payment portal. Every reminder should include a direct payment link. Clients who have to log into a separate system or email you to ask how to pay will delay. A one-click portal embedded in the reminder email removes that friction entirely.

- Set up reconciliation sync. Connect your invoicing tool to QuickBooks or Xero so payments auto-match to open invoices. This eliminates the weekly manual matching session and gives you an accurate real-time view of outstanding AR.

- Review your DSO after the first full billing cycle. DSO is your average number of days from invoice sent to payment received. Baseline it before you start, then check it 30 and 60 days after turning on automation. Most agencies see a meaningful reduction within the first cycle.

If your agency connects billing with project delivery, pair this workflow with your client onboarding setup. Our post on AI for client onboarding automation shows how to build a single connected workflow from contract signing through to the first invoice delivery.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can AI send payment reminders automatically?

Yes. Tools like BILL, FreshBooks, and HoneyBook can automatically send reminder emails at configurable intervals before and after a due date, without any manual input from you. You write the reminder templates once, set the schedule, and the system sends them every time an invoice ages past the threshold you define.

### Is AI invoicing different from my current accounting software?

Most small agencies already use QuickBooks, Xero, or FreshBooks for accounting. AI invoicing builds on top of these tools: it adds predictive payment timing, automated follow-up sequences, and collections prioritization that basic invoicing modules do not include. You typically connect an AI AR layer to your existing accounting software rather than replacing it.

### How long does an overdue invoice follow-up sequence take to set up?

Most platforms let you configure a basic follow-up sequence in under an hour. You define the trigger (invoice not paid by due date), the intervals (reminder at 3 days, 7 days, 14 days), and the message templates. After that, the system handles every overdue invoice automatically with no per-invoice effort from you.

### Will automated payment reminders damage client relationships?

Not if they are written in a professional tone and timed reasonably. Most clients appreciate a clear, consistent reminder rather than an awkward phone call. A well-written sequence that starts gently and escalates only after two or three missed reminders is less disruptive to the relationship than irregular manual follow-up or silence. You remain in control of the message content and can always pause the sequence for a specific client.

### What is DSO and how does AI reduce it?

DSO stands for days sales outstanding: the average number of days between sending an invoice and receiving payment. AI reduces DSO by predicting which invoices are likely to go overdue so you can follow up earlier, automating reminder sequences so no invoice falls through the cracks, and offering clients a self-serve payment portal that removes friction from the payment step itself. Quadient reports a 34% reduction in DSO for organizations using AI-assisted AR workflows.

## Get Your Agency Billing Running on Autopilot

Our workflow automation service can set up your invoice triggers, reminder sequences, and payment portal so the entire billing cycle runs without manual intervention. Our AI consulting service can audit your current billing process and identify exactly where time and revenue are slipping through the gaps.

If your agency also uses outbound sales, explore Pulse , FaithlineAI's sales platform, to keep your pipeline moving while your billing workflow handles collection automatically. Or book a free call to walk through your current billing setup and find the fastest path to getting paid on time.

For freelancers, who often juggle multiple clients, contracts, and payment timelines, efficient payment tracking is essential. With 72% of freelancers using invoicing software to streamline payment collection, it's clear that automated solutions are in demand. AI-powered invoicing tools have revolutionized payment tracking for small businesses. These tools offer real-time tracking of payments, helping businesses stay on top of their finances. ### Benefits of AI-Powered Payment Tracking

The ability to generate detailed financial reports automatically saves small businesses time and allows them to focus on growth and client work.

By reducing manual errors and the time spent on these tasks, small businesses can free up valuable time to focus on other important areas of their business. Automating these tasks allows them to reclaim more time for client projects and revenue-generating activities.

feasibility.testing: Use Postman collections to script sandbox invoice creation with past due dates and to post mocked webhook payloads to your endpoint. Unit-test escalation logic (reminder count -> tone level) and split math (amounts sum exactly, currency rounding). Snapshot-test Claude reply classification against ~10 hand-written client replies with JSON schema validation. Do one end-to-end sandbox run: create invoice, pay with sandbox buyer, confirm webhook stops follow-ups.

complexity.rationale: Core loop (list invoices, detect overdue, draft with Claude, approve, send) is moderate. Hard parts: ingesting client replies (PayPal invoicing has no inbound reply channel, so email inbound parsing is needed), split-invoice creation/cancellation semantics, webhook verification, and tone learning. sponsorUsage is empty but sponsor tech is required, so integration work is added.

feasibility.deployment: Deploy Next.js on Render as a web service with Postgres or SQLite-on-disk for state (invoices, reminder history, approvals). Render cron job runs overdue scan. Register the Render URL as the PayPal webhook listener. Keep secrets in Render env vars. Deploy by end of day 1 so webhook registration is tested early.

idea_versions.name: PayNudge
idea_versions.summary: PayNudge is an AI collections assistant for freelancers who invoice through PayPal. It watches for overdue invoices, drafts tone-matched reminders, proposes split payments when clients can't pay in full, and stops follow-ups once payment is confirmed. Every send needs the freelancer's one-tap approval.
idea_versions.userProblem: Freelancers lose weeks chasing overdue invoices and dislike writing awkward reminder emails.
idea_versions.targetAudience: Freelancers who invoice clients through PayPal.
idea_versions.workflow: The freelancer connects PayNudge to PayPal Invoicing (sandbox), and PayNudge monitors which invoices are overdue. For each overdue invoice it drafts a reminder in the freelancer's own tone, friendly at first and firmer on later reminders. If a client replies that they can't pay in full, the agent reads the reply, proposes splitting the amount, and creates new PayPal invoices for each part. Nothing is sent until the freelancer approves it with one tap. When PayPal reports the payment via a webhook, PayNudge marks the invoice settled and stops the follow-ups.

idea_versions.originalPitch: PayNudge is an AI collections assistant for freelancers who invoice through PayPal. Freelancers lose weeks chasing overdue invoices and hate writing awkward reminder emails. PayNudge connects to PayPal Invoicing in the sandbox, watches which invoices are overdue, and drafts a reminder in the freelancer's own tone — friendly first, firmer later. If a client replies that they can't pay in full, the agent proposes splitting the amount and creates new PayPal invoices for each part, but nothing is sent until the freelancer approves it with one tap. When PayPal reports the payment through a webhook, PayNudge marks the invoice settled and stops the follow-ups. Built with Next.js, the PayPal Invoicing and Webhooks APIs in sandbox mode, and Claude for drafting and reading client replies.

Nothing is built yet, though, and the hardest piece is unspecified. The stack has no email inbox integration, so it is unclear how PayNudge receives client replies. The split-payment step also has to handle the original invoice, or the client may be billed twice.
suggestions: Specify the reply channel, for example an inbound email webhook or a paste-in reply box for the demo.
Cancel or annotate the original invoice before issuing split invoices, and show this explicitly.
Check whether PayPal invoices already support partial payments natively; if so, explain why separate invoices are better or use the native feature.
Use the sandbox webhook simulator to make the paid-invoice event reproducible.

suggestions: Design a single dashboard listing overdue invoices with a pending-approval queue.

Cover at least one non-happy path (client disputes or ignores the reminder).

gaps: No data or sources on how common overdue invoices are or how much time chasing them costs.
No user-reported experience or interviews with freelancers.

opening.text: Automated payment reminders are a well-worn feature category, and LLM-drafted polite emails are now commonplace. build_tasks.description: Create the Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) repo with an OSS license, add env var placeholders (PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID, PAYPAL_SECRET, PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL), set up SQLite/Postgres via Prisma with tables for invoices, reminders, approvals and replies, and deploy to Render with a /api/health route.
build_tasks.acceptance: Public Render HTTPS URL serves the landing page; /api/health returns 200 with DB connectivity true; repo is public on GitHub with a LICENSE visible in About.

build_tasks.title: Build the AG Grid invoice and approval queue as the primary input surface
build_tasks.description: Use AG Grid as the main workspace: rows are overdue invoices with columns for client, amount, days overdue, reminder level and draft status. Freelancers act from the grid itself: inline-edit tone level, select rows to generate drafts, and approve/reject via a row action button.
build_tasks.acceptance: Dashboard renders an AG Grid fed from the DB; selecting rows and clicking 'Draft reminders' triggers the draft API for those IDs; inline tone-level edits persist after reload; the approve action is an AG Grid cell renderer.

build_tasks.title: Sync PayPal sandbox invoices and flag overdue ones
build_tasks.description: Implement OAuth client-credentials token fetch, list/search invoices via the Invoicing v2 API, upsert into the DB, and mark invoices overdue when status is unpaid/sent and due date < today. Add a Postman collection that seeds sandbox invoices with past due dates. Expose a POST /api/sync endpoint usable by a Render cron job.
build_tasks.acceptance: Running the Postman seed and then /api/sync shows at least 3 seeded past-due invoices flagged overdue in the grid; paid or future-dated invoices are not flagged; repeated syncs create no duplicates.

build_tasks.title: Generate Claude reminder drafts in the freelancer's tone with 3 escalation levels
build_tasks.description: Settings page accepts 1-3 pasted sample emails. The draft endpoint calls Claude with these samples as few-shot style and a tone level (1 friendly, 2 firm-polite, 3 firm with payment deadline) derived from prior sent reminder count. It returns JSON {subject, body}, stored as a pending draft.
build_tasks.acceptance: For an invoice with 0, 1 and 2 prior reminders, drafts are produced at levels 1, 2 and 3 respectively, each including invoice number, amount and pay link; a unit test covers the count→level mapping; output is validated against a schema.

build_tasks.title: Classify pasted client replies with Claude into structured intent
build_tasks.description: Add a paste-reply box per invoice. Claude returns JSON {intent: will_pay|cant_pay_full|dispute|other, proposedParts?: number, notes} validated with zod. Store the reply and classification and display them in the invoice row detail.
build_tasks.acceptance: A test set of 10 hand-written replies all return schema-valid JSON, with at least 9/10 having correct intent; a cant_pay_full reply surfaces a 'Propose split' action in the UI.

build_tasks.title: Propose split payment and create PayPal split invoices
build_tasks.description: For a cant_pay_full reply, compute a 2-3 part split (exact cents, remainder on the last part, staggered due dates) and show it as a pending approval. On approval, create N draft invoices via Invoicing v2, then cancel the original to avoid double payment, linking children to the parent in the DB.
build_tasks.acceptance: A unit test proves part amounts sum exactly to the original total; after approval the sandbox shows N new invoices and the original as CANCELLED; the grid shows the parent→child relationship.

build_tasks.title: Enforce one-tap approval gate for every outbound action
build_tasks.description: All sends (reminders and split invoice sends) go through an approvals table with status pending/approved/rejected. A single Approve tap executes the action (PayPal send/remind endpoint); no code path sends without an approved record. Log the timestamp and result.
build_tasks.acceptance: Pending drafts never reach PayPal (verified by sandbox showing no reminder); one tap on Approve sends it and updates the status to sent within 5s; rejected items are not sent; the audit log lists each action.

build_tasks.title: Handle PayPal paid webhooks to settle invoices and stop follow-ups
build_tasks.description: Implement POST /api/webhooks/paypal that verifies the signature via the verify-webhook-signature API, handles INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID (verify the name), marks the invoice settled, and cancels pending reminder drafts. Add a 'Simulate payment' demo button and a Postman mocked event, plus polling fallback in the sync.
build_tasks.acceptance: Paying a sandbox invoice with the buyer account marks it settled in the grid and removes pending drafts; invalid signatures return 400; the simulate button produces the same outcome; settled invoices are excluded from future drafts.

build_tasks.title: Run the full end-to-end loop in sandbox and log findings
build_tasks.description: Execute seed → sync → draft → approve → paste reply → split → pay → webhook on the deployed app, ideally with one other freelancer. Record issues, fix blockers, and save notes and screenshots in docs/testing.md.
build_tasks.acceptance: At least one complete loop succeeds on the Render URL; docs/testing.md lists each step's result, bugs found and their fixes.

build_tasks.title: Write the submission text description
build_tasks.description: Summarize the problem, the workflow, features, AG Grid usage, the human-in-the-loop design, and the tech stack.
build_tasks.acceptance: The description covers all 6 features and sponsor usage, and is pasted into the submission draft.

build_tasks.title: Publish hosted demo URL and run instructions
build_tasks.description: Confirm the Render demo is live with seeded data, and write README setup steps (env vars, Prisma migrate, Postman seed, webhook registration).
build_tasks.acceptance: A fresh clone following the README runs locally; the hosted URL loads the seeded dashboard.

build_tasks.title: Finalize the public repository
build_tasks.description: Ensure all source, Postman collection and assets are committed, secrets are removed, and the LICENSE is visible.
build_tasks.acceptance: The repo is public, the license shows in About, and a secret scan finds no keys.

build_tasks.title: Record a sub-3-minute demo video
build_tasks.description: Show the grid, a tone-escalated draft, one-tap approval, reply → split invoices in PayPal sandbox, and payment → settled. Upload publicly to YouTube.
build_tasks.acceptance: The video is under 3:00, public, and shows every core step working.

build_tasks.title: Document test credentials
build_tasks.description: Add sandbox buyer login and demo access details to the README or submission notes.
build_tasks.acceptance: A judge can log into the sandbox buyer account and pay a demo invoice using the provided info.

build_tasks.title: Complete the submission form
build_tasks.description: Fill in all required fields with links to the repo, demo and video.
build_tasks.acceptance: The submission shows as submitted before the deadline.

segments.title: The problem
segments.onScreen: Title card: 'Freelancers lose weeks chasing overdue invoices.' Simple illustration of an inbox full of unsent reminder drafts.
segments.narration: If you freelance and invoice through PayPal, you know the routine: the invoice goes out, the due date passes, and then you spend weeks writing reminder emails you hate sending. That is time not spent on paid work.

segments.title: Who it's for and the idea
segments.onScreen: Slide: target audience (freelancers using PayPal invoicing) and the design principle 'Human-in-the-loop: you approve every send.' Label the slide 'Planned design'.
segments.narration: PayNudge is designed for freelancers who invoice clients through PayPal. The idea is an AI collections assistant that helps with overdue invoices while keeping the freelancer in control. The core principle is that nothing goes out without the freelancer's approval.

segments.title: Where we are
segments.onScreen: Slide: 'Status: in development, no live demo yet.' Tech stack logos: Next.js, PayPal sandbox, Claude.
segments.narration: We are being upfront: we don't have working features to demo yet. Rather than show mockups as if they were real, we are presenting the problem, our planned approach, and the stack we chose: Next.js, PayPal's sandbox Invoicing and Webhooks APIs, and Claude.

segments.title: What's next
segments.onScreen: Roadmap slide: '1. First working flow on the PayPal sandbox. 2. Test with freelancers. 3. Share measured results.'
segments.narration: Our next milestone is getting a first end-to-end flow working against the PayPal sandbox, then testing it with real freelancers and reporting what we actually measure.

demo_plans.closing: PayNudge: so freelancers spend less time chasing payments and more time doing the work. Thanks for watching.

# AgroWise

AgroWise fuses low-cost root-zone sensors with AI and IVR to provide precision farming via any phone. It blocks banned chemicals and cuts water use by 40%, reaching the 50% of farmers without 4G.

Like

Comment

#### Submission history

## Inspiration

Indian farmers are making life-or-death crop decisions blind .

Root-zone moisture deficits, pH imbalances, and early fungal infections happen underground, invisible to the naked eye. By the time a crop wilts, the physiological damage is already permanent. The farmer then over-waters or under-waters, triggering a vicious cycle of root rot or stunting.

The numbers tell a brutal story:

- 146 million smallholder farmers in India

- 1 extension officer per 1,000+ farmers

- Soil testing takes days and costs money

- Weather apps give 20km averages , missing the micro-climate that triggers blight on a specific field

- Most agritech apps need a smartphone + 4G . Half of rural India has neither.

We started AgroWise with a simple question: What if every farmer, smartphone or feature phone, could see what's happening underground, in real time, in their own language?

## What it does

AgroWise is a three-layer phygital precision agriculture system that bridges the digital divide:

### Layer 1: AgroSense Spike (Hardware)

A solar-powered, deploy-and-forget IoT sensor (ESP32-based) that sits in the root zone measuring soil moisture, temperature, and humidity every 30 minutes. Under ₹800 BOM. No buttons, no battery swaps, no maintenance. Spikes communicate via LoRa long-range radio to a shared village gateway hub with a single SIM card, one hub serves 50–100 farmers.

### Layer 2: AgroWise App (Software + AI)

A Progressive Web App featuring:

- "Soil Thirst" gauge , visual, intuitive, no jargon

- Action cards , "Water Field Today" or "Hold Off" (not percentages)

- AI-powered disease diagnosis that combines leaf photos WITH soil sensor data for higher accuracy. A yellowing leaf might look like nutrient deficiency, but if soil humidity is high, it's actually fungal stress, our system catches this.

- AgroMind conversational agent that remembers your farm history across sessions, crop stage, past diagnoses, seasonal patterns

- CIBRC safety filter , every AI response is checked against a government database of 448 chemicals (88 banned). Banned substances are architecturally blocked , not just flagged.

### Layer 3: Kisan-Vani IVR (Voice)

Toll-free voice alerts in Hindi, Bengali, and Odia for feature-phone farmers. Zero internet, zero app required. The system proactively CALLS the farmer when soil crosses critical thresholds. Works on any phone that can receive a call, even a ₹500 feature phone on a 2G network.

## How we built it

### AI Architecture

We use an agentic architecture with intent-based tool binding, not a simple chatbot.

- Intent Classifier (Claude 3.5 Sonnet via TrueFoundry, ~8 tokens) categorizes farmer queries into 11 intent categories

- Based on intent, only relevant tools are bound to the main agent (Gemini 2.5 Flash via Vertex AI). A weather query can't accidentally trigger pesticide recommendations.

- The agent runs a tool loop (max 6 iterations) gathering data from IMD weather APIs, Agmarknet mandi prices, ICAR knowledge base, and 221K KCC farmer Q&A transcripts indexed in ChromaDB

- A mandatory CIBRC post-filter scans every response for banned chemicals using regex word-boundary matching before it reaches the farmer

For disease diagnosis, Gemini 2.5 Vision analyzes leaf photos alongside real-time soil sensor data, this neuro-symbolic fusion is what distinguishes us from image-only solutions like Plantix.

### RAG Pipeline

Intent-aware retrieval across two ChromaDB collections:

- ICAR knowledge base (soil testing manuals, crop nutrition guides)

- KCC transcripts (221K+ real farmer Q&As from data.gov.in, licensed under GODL-India)

Embeddings: Vertex AI text-embedding-005 (768 dimensions). Relevance threshold: 0.3. Deduplication by first 100 characters.

### IoT & Connectivity

- Spike → Hub : LoRa 868 MHz radio (2–5 km range in open fields)

- Hub → Cloud : 4G/2G cellular (Jio IoT SIM, ₹49–99/month)

- Hub serves : 50–100 spikes. Cost per spike per month: ₹1–2.

- Offline resilience : Spike buffers 7 days of readings locally. App uses Redux Persist for offline caching.

### Mobile

React Native + Expo for cross-platform delivery. Action-card UI designed for low-literacy farmers, icons over text, voice readout for alerts.

### Voice (IVR)

Sarvam AI for text-to-speech in Indic languages. Threshold-triggered outbound calls via toll-free number.

### Testing

272 unit tests (all passing), deliberately mocked (no live API calls). Separate integration scripts for live IMD/Agmarknet connections. Tests validate intent routing, safety filtering, tool binding logic.

## Challenges we ran into

-
Hardware survivability across Indian climates : India ranges from 48°C Rajasthan deserts to -15°C Kashmir winters to 3000mm Kerala monsoons. We solved this with IP67-sealed ABS housing, capacitive sensors that read through the housing wall (never touching soil directly), and supercapacitors instead of lithium batteries.

-
Connectivity in rural India : WiFi is useless in open fields (30m range). Putting a SIM in every spike costs ₹100/month/spike. Our breakthrough was the hub-and-spoke LoRa architecture , spikes use long-range radio to a shared gateway. One SIM serves an entire village.

-
Building farmer trust : Sontu Da told us directly, "I have seen people come with tablets and apps before and nothing ever worked." What convinced him was the spike physically going into his soil and showing data he couldn't see. The physical device creates trust that software alone cannot.

-
Language accessibility : 7 of 12 test farmers rated English-only screens as unusable . We defaulted to Hindi/Bengali from login and made language our highest-priority design decision. It became our highest-rated feature (4.7/5).

-
LLM safety in agriculture : An AI hallucinating a banned chemical name could cause real harm, poisoned soil, health damage. We built two independent safety gates : the CIBRC tool-level check AND a post-response regex filter. Even if the LLM hallucinates, the filter catches it.

## Accomplishments that we're proud of

- Field-tested with 12 real farmers in Kharagpur, West Bengal, in Hindi and Bengali

- Trust rating: 4.6/5 (memory feature was highest rated)

- Language accessibility: 4.7/5 , our highest-rated feature

- Intent to continue using: 83% (10 of 12 farmers said yes)

- Sontu Da's story : Was about to buy unnecessary fertilizer. Our system combined his leaf photo with soil data and correctly identified fungal stress from humidity, not nutrient deficiency. Saved his money. Saved his crop.

- 272 unit tests passing on the backend

- Won NSCIF 2026 (National Student Change Initiatives Fest), 1st place, ₹50,000 prize, organized by Connecting Dreams Foundation & Ashoka at EMPI Business School, New Delhi

- Spike BOM under ₹800 , less than a bag of DAP fertilizer

## What we learned

The biggest lesson wasn't technical, it was entrepreneurial .

We walked into NSCIF 2026 as engineers who built a working prototype. On Day 1, the jury grilled us on hardware feasibility across Indian climates, sensor deployment density, rural connectivity, and business model viability. We stumbled on some answers. We corrected course overnight, rebuilt our hardware narrative, designed the hub-and-spoke connectivity model, and mapped the distribution strategy through existing Krishi Vigyan Kendra networks.

Day 2, we came back with answers grounded in reality, not just code.

Key learning : Engineers build systems. Entrepreneurs build trust. The spike physically going into a farmer's soil creates more trust than any demo deck ever could.

We also learned that Responsible AI isn't a feature you add, it's how you architect from day one. The CIBRC safety filter, the mandatory tool enforcement, the source-cited responses, these aren't afterthoughts. They're structural decisions that make the difference between a research project and a system farmers can actually trust with their livelihoods.

## What's next for AgroWise

- Pilot deployment : 500 spikes across 3 villages in West Bengal (Month 1–6)

- Injection-molded housing + PCB assembly , moving from hand-soldered prototypes to production hardware with IP67 certification

- LoRa gateway firmware and hub management dashboard

- B2G district dashboards , aggregated soil health data for agricultural extension officers

- Expand language support via Sarvam AI to cover more Indic languages

- Nutrient sensing module (NPK add-on, ₹400 extra) in v3.0

- Target: 50,000+ farmers through KVK networks across West Bengal and Odisha within 36 months

# Inspiration

This project was born from a very personal experience. During my summer vacation, I went to my village and saw my grandfather, who is a farmer, struggling to sell his crops. He had to travel a long distance to the mandi, only to face middlemen who forced him to sell at unfairly low prices. Seeing his hard work undervalued broke my heart. That’s when I decided to create a solution that could help farmers like him get the fair value they truly deserve.

# What it does

KisanSetu is a platform that directly connects farmers to buyers — cutting out the middlemen. Farmers can list their produce, and buyers such as retailers, wholesalers, or food processors can purchase directly from them. This ensures fair pricing, transparency, and trust, while also reducing exploitation.

# How we built it

We used AI-powered matching systems to connect farmers and buyers efficiently. IBM’s Granite models, data preprocessing tools, and agent frameworks helped us design an intelligent platform. We also integrated a simple and user-friendly interface so that even first-time digital users could easily navigate the system.

# Challenges we ran into

Ensuring that the platform is simple enough for rural farmers to use. Handling multiple languages and voice support for inclusivity. Building trust among farmers who have been exploited for years. Designing a system that could work even with limited internet access. Accomplishments that we're proud of Turning a personal problem into a real, scalable solution. Designing an inclusive platform that works for small farmers, not just large ones. Creating an AI-powered system that balances technology with simplicity. Building something that could truly make an impact on rural livelihoods.

# What we learned

We learned how important empathy is in innovation. Technology alone isn’t enough; understanding the struggles of real people shapes better solutions. We also gained experience in AI model integration, user-centric design, and building trust through transparency.

# What's next for KisanSetu

We plan to expand KisanSetu by: Adding voice-based features for non-literate farmers. Integrating payment gateways for secure transactions. Partnering with government and NGOs to scale outreach. Building a logistics support system to make crop delivery seamless.

# 🌾 CropGuard: AI-Powered Crop Disease Dignosis

Event: DevLaunch Hackathon 2026 (WPBrigade × iCodeGuru)

CropGuard is a multi-modal AI-powered system designed to assist traditional farmers by detecting crop diseases from leaf images and providing spoken Urdu guidance . The platform leverages state-of-the-art computer vision, natural language processing, and speech synthesis to make advanced agricultural intelligence accessible to non-technical users.

The system allows farmers to simply upload a crop image. The AI then identifies the crop and disease, explains the issue in English, translates the result into Urdu, and finally converts it into natural Urdu voice output , enabling farmers to interact with the system without needing literacy or technical skills.

## 🎯 Project Overview

CropGuard addresses a real-world problem in agriculture:

farmers lack instant access to expert-level crop disease diagnosis.

By using modern AI models, CropGuard provides:

- Crop name detection

- Disease identification

- Confidence score

- Disease description

- Recommended pesticide

- Urdu text guidance

- Urdu voice assistance (hands-free)

This project demonstrates an end-to-end multi-modal AI system combining:

- Vision AI

- NLP translation

- Speech synthesis

Built as a hackathon demo , but architected to be scalable and production-ready .

## 🧠 AI Model & Intelligence Pipeline

### Gemini Flash 3 (Vision AI)

Gemini Flash 3 is a lightweight and high-performance multimodal model capable of understanding images and generating structured textual outputs.

In CropGuard, Gemini Flash 3 is used to:

- Analyze crop leaf images

- Identify crop type

- Detect disease patterns

- Generate human-readable diagnosis

### Language & Voice Intelligence

After vision inference:

- Output is generated in English

- Gemini Translation API converts English → Urdu

- Google Voice API converts Urdu text → natural Urdu speech

This enables:

- Voice-based interaction

- Accessibility for illiterate farmers

- Real-world usability in rural Pakistan

## 📊 Supported Crops

CropGuard is designed to work with multiple crop types , including but not limited to:

- Wheat

- Rice

- Cotton

- Tomato

- Potato

- Sugarcane

- Maize

- Vegetables and fruits

The system is model-agnostic and can scale to more crops without retraining.

## 🔬 Testing & Evaluation

Since this project is based on real-time AI inference (no custom training) , evaluation was performed through:

- Manual testing on multiple crop images

- Cross-verification with online agricultural sources

- Live testing during hackathon demo

The system demonstrated:

- High confidence predictions for common crops

- Accurate disease identification for visible symptoms

- Consistent translation and voice generation

This validates CropGuard as a practical real-world AI assistant , not just a theoretical model.

feasibility.testing: Collect 5–10 real or recorded Odia and Hindi voice clips and 10–15 crop photos from public datasets (e.g., rice leaf disease and PlantVillage-style images). Use them to measure STT accuracy and sanity-check diagnoses. Unit-test the KALIA rules engine with edge-case profiles. Manually test audio recording on an Android Chrome phone, since iOS Safari MediaRecorder formats differ. Ideally have an Odia speaker review the generated text.

complexity.rationale: Core pipeline (Odia/Hindi STT → multimodal LLM diagnosis → simple-language reply, optionally TTS) is mostly glue code around hosted models, but Odia speech recognition quality is uncertain, KVK data must be compiled manually, and KALIA eligibility rules need careful encoding from official sources. Three distinct features plus a chat UI is a lot for ~30 hours.

feasibility.deployment: Deploy the Next.js app to Vercel, using API routes as server-side proxies so API keys stay hidden. Store the KVK data and KALIA rules as static JSON. No database is needed. Watch serverless body-size limits for audio and images by compressing images client-side and keeping clips short (under about 30s).
assumptions: 1–2 developers comfortable with Next.js and calling hosted AI APIs
API keys for an LLM and STT provider are obtained in the first hour
Odia STT is accepted as best-effort, with an editable transcript

integrations.name: Speech-to-text for Odia/Hindi
integrations.notes: Hindi is widely supported. Odia support and accuracy vary by provider. Options include OpenAI Whisper (Odia accuracy reportedly weak), Google Cloud Speech-to-Text (verify the official API for the or-IN locale), and AI4Bharat IndicConformer or Bhashini, which are Indic-focused; verify the official API and access process for Bhashini. Test with real Odia audio early.

integrations.name: Multimodal LLM for image + text diagnosis
integrations.notes: Use a hosted vision-capable model such as GPT-4o-class or Gemini-class. Prompt it to return structured JSON with likely conditions, confidence, simple next steps and a referral to a KVK. Outputs must be framed as suggestions rather than diagnoses. Generating Odia text output is feasible but needs native-speaker review.

integrations.name: Krishi Vigyan Kendra directory
integrations.notes: Odisha has roughly 30+ KVKs, about one per district. Hand-curate a static JSON file of district → KVK name and phone from ICAR/OUAT public listings. Use a district dropdown or browser geolocation plus district centroids. Do not depend on a live API.

integrations.name: KALIA eligibility check
integrations.notes: There is no confident public eligibility API, so verify the official API before relying on one. Implement a rule-based questionnaire built from published scheme criteria (land size or landless status, cultivator category, income-tax payer and government-employee exclusions, etc.). Show a disclaimer and link to the official portal. Rules may have changed, so cite the source date.

integrations.name: Optional text-to-speech reply
integrations.notes: Voice output matters for non-readers. Odia TTS availability varies by provider, so verify before committing. Use Hindi TTS as a fallback.
